data.title: HeartSciences Shareholders Approve Proposed Business Combination with Fortitude Mining
data.description:
Transaction remains subject to Nasdaq approval and other closing conditions

SOUTHLAKE, Texas, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HeartSciences Inc. (Nasdaq: HSCS; HSCSW) ("HeartSciences" or the "Company"), a healthcare information technology ("HIT") company focused on advancing electrocardiography ("ECG" or "EKG") through the integration of artificial intelligence ("AI"), today announced that its shareholders approved the proposed business combination (the “Proposed Transaction”) with Fortitude Mining Holdings, Inc. (“Fortitude”) at the Company’s special meeting of shareholders held today.

Detailed voting results for the proposals considered at the special meeting will be reported in a Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

“We appreciate the participation and support of our shareholders,” said Andrew Simpson, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of HeartSciences. “Today’s vote is an important step toward completing our proposed business combination with Fortitude. We are working with Fortitude to satisfy the remaining closing conditions and will provide an update when the transaction closes.”

Upon completion of the Proposed Transaction, the combined company is expected to operate as Fortitude Mining Group, Inc., and its Class A common stock is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol “TUDE,” subject to Nasdaq approval. Completion of the transaction remains subject to the applicable listing requirements and other closing conditions under the merger agreement.

About Fortitude

Fortitude is establishing a new category of public infrastructure as a premier vertically-integrated Zcash mining platform. Following the expected closing of its business combination with HeartSciences, Fortitude is preparing to commence trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker TUDE. Like Bitcoin, Zcash relies on secure proof of work mining, but it is designed to power the privacy economy by validating transactions without exposing underlying financial data. Upon its market debut, Fortitude believes it will offer investors a regulated vehicle for direct exposure to this growing ecosystem. Driven by a seasoned management team, Fortitude pairs self-mining operations with an owned data center footprint and a controlled power portfolio to scale high conviction opportunities across the broader digital asset landscape.

For more information, visit Fortitude Mining and follow Fortitude on X at @FortitudeCrypto

In the ordinary course of business, Fortitude currently sells or otherwise monetizes all the digital assets that it mines, including ZEC. In addition, Fortitude and its affiliates and subsidiaries, including DCG, from time to time sell, pledge or otherwise monetize their digital asset holdings, including ZEC. The funds received from such sales, pledges, or other monetization activities are used to fund operating expenses and capital investments, as well as for other purposes, including to hedge exposures and realize investment gains.

About HeartSciences Inc.

HeartSciences is a healthcare information technology company advancing the use of electrocardiography ("ECG" or "EKG") through the integration of artificial intelligence. HeartSciences' MyoVista Insights™ platform is a device-agnostic ECG management system designed to improve clinical efficiency and decision-making. Its MyoVista wavECG device is designed to deliver conventional ECG functionality while supporting AI-enabled solutions.

For more information, visit www.heartsciences.com

data.title: Danaher Collaborates with Microsoft to Make Scientific Instruments Agentically Connected and Laboratories More Intelligent
data.description:
Advancing autonomous science through smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Danaher Corporation () today announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft to support the development of smart scientific instruments and an interoperable agentic ecosystem that connects technologies across Danaher while remaining open to the broader laboratory ecosystem, helping scientists move from scientific questions to experimental evidence faster. The partnership seeks to combine Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise with Microsoft's AI technologies, making experimental execution more streamlined and insights more readily available to translate discovery into human impact.

The partnership is focused on accelerating the development of a common agentic platform for instrument control and insight generation. The platform is built on Microsoft technology: Microsoft Azure for secure, compliant cloud infrastructure, and Microsoft Foundry to power the AI agents that interpret results and guide instrument control. Its goal is to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation, while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories.

While the companies are continuing to develop this platform, the first commercial applications will reach Danaher customers this year, including MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant, Molecular Devices' software for its high-content cellular imaging systems, designed to provide product support. Additional next-generation, agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use this platform are planned for 2027.

"Danaher's businesses bring deep scientific and instrument expertise to customers every day," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, President and CEO of Danaher. "With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher. Through context and learning, that foundation can continuously inform the next experiment and the best analysis. This partnership is an important step toward making laboratories not just connected, but intelligent."

As part of this partnership, smart, agent-enabled instruments are being designed with the goal of supporting scientists across four critical activities:

  • Translating scientific intent into experimental plans, instrument setup and methods
  • Controlling instrument hardware within defined safety boundaries and with user oversight, while guiding execution and troubleshooting
  • Interpreting results and identifying quality issues in real time
  • Recommending corrective actions and next experiments for scientist review

AI-assisted instruments are intended to simplify complex scientific workflows. In preliminary internal testing, novice scientists conducting an AI-assisted experiment on a Leica microscope took up to 83% less time and up to 68% fewer steps to complete than a novice working without the AI assistant, while producing high-quality data and completing the experiment in a time comparable to an expert.

"Danaher's scientific expertise, combined with Microsoft's AI platform, aims to give scientists more choice and control, and more time for discovery," said Deb Cupp, Executive Vice President and Chief Revenue Officer, Microsoft Global Enterprise. "This partnership aligns with our goal to help translate AI into real-world impact."

The partnership is designed to advance Danaher's broader strategy for AI and autonomous science by connecting intelligence at the instrument with data, laboratory workflows and the physical execution of experiments. Intelligent instruments are a first step. As instruments and laboratory systems become more connected and interoperable, Danaher believes experimental results can help scientists determine what to do next, supporting discovery through increasingly connected and autonomous workflows under scientific oversight.

data.title: Oil Prices Retreat as Traders Assess Supply Outlook, Middle East Risks — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Farhan Rafid

DOHA, Qatar--Oil prices retreated Friday after earlier gains as traders assessed improving global supply conditions and continued threats to Middle Eastern oil shipments.

Brent crude futures fell 0.7% to $91.36 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate declined 1% to $82.40 a barrel.

Both benchmarks have fallen around 15% so far this month as U.S. President Trump held off on renewed large-scale strikes against Iran. A stronger U.S. dollar and broader weakness across commodity markets have also added to pressure on oil prices.

Oil shipments through major Middle Eastern chokepoints rose 19% in the third quarter from the previous three months, according to a report published Thursday by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. The agency said regional crude production reached 23.1 million barrels a day in October, the highest since the conflict began, as producers expand shipments through alternative routes. The EIA expects Brent to average $86 a barrel next year as recovering supplies help rebuild global inventories.

The agency said shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and Suez Canal increased, while flows through the Bab el-Mandeb declined. Preliminary shipping data from Vortexa indicated that shipments remained near third-quarter levels in October.

Steadily increasing oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz had contributed to the recent decline in crude prices, the EIA said. The agency expects global oil inventories to increase as Middle Eastern production and exports recover, while oil demand remains relatively flat in the near term.

The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that Israel's spy chief had urged U.S. officials to support renewed strikes against Iran, while Gulf countries pressed for negotiations amid concerns about retaliatory attacks on regional infrastructure. President Trump is weighing whether to resume a broader military campaign against Tehran.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia said Thursday that a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh's financial district, with no injuries reported, according to the Saudi Press Agency. The Wall Street Journal identified the building as the headquarters of the kingdom's Public Investment Fund.

Pavel Molchanov, an investment strategist at Raymond James, said Thursday that oil markets have become increasingly accustomed to periodic tensions in the Middle East, provided they don't escalate into a broader conflict. He said production among OPEC's Persian Gulf members had recovered to 87% of prewar levels as the industry adapted to disruptions.

The International Energy Agency said Thursday that the response in oil prices to the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz had been less severe than the scale of the supply shock might have suggested, amid ample global supply and well-stocked inventories.

In its World Energy Outlook, the agency said the global oil market was expected to return to a surplus as Middle Eastern production recovered faster than demand. It projects an oversupply of 1.7 million barrels a day in the fourth quarter, widening to about 3.8 million barrels a day next year.

The agency also said prolonged disruptions to shipping through the strait could accelerate investment in alternative export routes, with around 7 million barrels a day of new pipeline capacity under construction or consideration. The projects would require an estimated $40 billion in investment, adding about $2 to the cost of each barrel of Middle Eastern oil exported.

Write to Farhan Rafid at farhan.rafid@wsj.com

data.title: The Container Store, A Neighborhood Intelligence Company, Announces Restoration of Its Systems Following Cybersecurity Incident
data.description:
Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc. () today announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, The Container Store, has restored its website and systems following a cybersecurity incident this past weekend.

Upon detecting suspicious activity, the company immediately activated its established cybersecurity protocols and proactively suspended online order-taking at The Container Store to protect its customer information and its systems. All retail locations remained open, serving customers through alternative transaction-processing procedures.

Marcus Lemonis, Chief Executive Officer of Neighborhood Intelligence, commented:

“I am extremely proud of how our technology and operational teams responded. We made the deliberate decision to prioritize the protection of our customers and our systems while keeping our stores open and serving customers. Our established protocols, combined with the expertise of our outside partners, allowed us to respond with discipline and restore operations in a controlled manner. I want to thank our associates and partners for their exceptional work and our customers for their patience and continued support.”

As part of its established response protocols, the company engaged leading independent cybersecurity experts to assist with the investigation, containment and restoration efforts. Our investigation into this event is ongoing, however we do not believe that this incident impacted the security of any customer financial data because The Container Store does not store or maintain consumer financial or payment information.

The company also maintains established risk mitigation procedures and business interruption insurance coverage designed to help manage operational and financial exposure associated with incidents of this nature.

The incident was isolated to The Container Store. We expect a minimal impact on consolidated revenue for the quarter, with any impact on profitability expected to be mitigated by our business interruption insurance. The company’s other businesses, including Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY and Kirkland’s, remained unaffected. The company continues to expect sequential revenue growth in the fourth quarter.

About Neighborhood Intelligence, Inc.

Neighborhood Intelligence (), previously Bed Bath & Beyond, Inc., is a data and technology company organized around three interconnected pillars: Omni-Channel Retail, Home Services and Home Ownership. Its portfolio includes Bed Bath & Beyond, Overstock, buybuy BABY, Kirkland’s, The Container Store, Elfa and Closet Works, along with its expanding Home Services and Home Ownership businesses. The Company also includes a blockchain asset portfolio inclusive of tZERO, GrainChain, and other assets. For more information, please visit neighborhoodintelligence.com.

data.title: Nvidia, AMD in focus as GF Securities says talk of server CPU cuts is 'overstated'
data.description:
Despite rumors that tech companies have started to cut orders for server CPUs, GF Securities said supply chain checks show just the opposite.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm said any talk that Meta and Microsoft have cut orders is inaccurate and that Meta has shifted some purchases of x86 to Nvidia's Grace and Vera server options. Additionally, Meta has accelerated general-server deployments for its Muse artificial intelligence agent.

For Microsoft, orders are unchanged, and any noise is simply reflecting original design manufacturer capacity allocations.

“Agentic workloads now account for ~80% of tokens on OpenRouter (weekly volume up 35x YoY), with GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol and Claude Duet supporting commercial adoption, while Meta Muse gained 11.2mn NA accounts in 7 weeks but saw Day-30 retention fall to 16.4%,” analysts at the firm wrote in a note to clients. “We maintain server CPU TAM of $211bn by 2030 (+47% CAGR), with 2027 unit growth of 29% (general servers +15%, AI-inference CPUs +79%) as agentic AI expands from 25% to 50% of total inference.”

The investment firm reiterated its Buy rating on AMD as it sees the Dr. Lisa Su-led company benefiting from a ramp in its Venice CPUs and continued share gains in x86 processors.

“We expect Venice to drive further share gains for AMD in the coming quarters, even outperforming Intel’s Diamond Rapids (set to launch by late 1Q27), on the back of superior perf-per-watt, large L3 SRAM, and up to 512 threads,” analysts at the firm added. “For now, we forecast Venice CPU shipments of 400k/5.4mn in 2026/2027, respectively.”

The firm also reiterated its Buy rating on Intel due to the company ramping up its Granite Rapids processors.

data.title: Westlake Agrees to Pay $199 Million to Settle Remaining PVC Pipe Antitrust Claims
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Westlake has agreed to pay a further $199 million to settle claims with two remaining plaintiff classes in U.S. PVC pipe price-fixing antitrust litigation, subject to court approval.

The chemical and building-products company said in recent filings that it agreed to pay $119.5 million to non-converter seller purchasers and $79.5 million to end-user plaintiffs.

Westlake, as well as other polyvinyl chloride, or PVC, pipe and fittings companies were defendants in a class action lawsuit between August of 2024 and June 2025 are alleged to have conspired with each other and price-reporting service OPIS to artificially inflate U.S. prices.

The latest settlement adds to a previously-approved $67 million settlement with direct purchasers.

Westlake noted that the settlements aren't meant to be admissions of liability or wrongdoing.

The company expects to record a pretax charge for substantially all of the $199 million in the fourth quarter.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: UK stocks fall as banks and energy shares drag in global risk-off mood
data.description:
UK's FTSE 100 was on track for its sharpest weekly decline in eight months on Friday, pressured by bank and energy shares as a weak global risk backdrop offset stronger-than-expected UK retail sales.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index CURRENCYCOM:UK100 fell 0.66 % to 10,383.6 points as of 1205 GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250 dropped 1.7%.

  • The financial sector was the biggest drag on the index, with HSBC Holdings off 2.3%, Standard Chartered down 3.9% and Barclays lower by 2.2%

  • Precious and industrial (.FTNMX551020) metal miners were on course for a loss of more than 10% this week, dragged down by softer gold and copper prices, making them among FTSE's worst-performing sectors

  • Shell dropped 1% and Ithaca Energy dropped nearly 5% as oil prices fell, with Brent crude (LCOC1) down about 1%, weighing on the sector

  • On the data front, UK retail sales volumes unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October from September, bolstered by a government call for households to stock up on long-life items as well as stronger clothing sales

  • Separately, UK government borrowing came in at £17 billion ($22.28 billion) in October, below forecasts of £18 billion, while earlier deficits were revised down by £3.6 billion, giving Chancellor John Healey some positive news on public finances

  • Meanwhile, Britain and the European Union were set to deepen ties through agreements on easing food trade and youth mobility at a summit on Friday, although broader questions about their long-term relationship remain in focus

  • Domestically-focused FTSE 250 was set for a seventh straight day of declines, marking its longest losing streak since an eight-session slide in November 2025

data.title: Fed hike bets hit Indonesia, Taiwan harder than India - IntelliNews Lambda
data.description:
Bets on a December rate rise by the US Federal Reserve are dragging Indonesia's rupiah and the Taiwan dollar towards multi-year lows, while India's rupee has so far been spared.

The dollar index reached 103.89 late on November 19, its highest since early April 2025 and almost 2% up on the month, Investing.com reported. Futures priced a quarter-point Fed rise at the December 8-9 meeting at about 94%, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller has argued for half a point.

The minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on November 18, gave traders more reason to bet. Almost all participants judged that further action to raise the target range, held at 3.75-4.00% in October with two dissenters wanting a rise, 'would likely be appropriate'. A couple said a move larger than 25 basis points could be considered at the next meeting if inflation data disappointed.

Jakarta faces a credibility problem made worse by politics, Taipei a flight of foreign equity money, and New Delhi an oil bill that has, for now, shrunk, so one strong dollar is testing each in a different place. The central banks have answered with three different tools: Bank Indonesia with rates, Taiwan's central bank with its reserves, and the Reserve Bank of India by taking dollar demand off the market.

Value against the US dollar, end of month, end-2024 = 100. Source: BIS via IntelliNews Lambda

Politics on top in Jakarta

The rupiah sank to a record of about 18,225 per dollar on November 12, according to Reuters, the day Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned after courts found his schooling papers fell short of election rules. It slid further, to 18,285 on November 17, before Bank Indonesia raised its policy rate to 6% the next day, taking its increases since May to 125 basis points. That decision and China's opposite problem were set side by side on November 19.

Bank Indonesia's reserves stood at $146.8bn at the end of October, its own figures show, against about $156.5bn at the end of 2025, the price of months of intervention. The rupiah was still near 18,260 on November 20, and the political calendar offers little relief: President Prabowo Subianto must send the People's Consultative Assembly two candidates by November 25 for the vacant post.

Policy rate on November 20, 2026, % and change since end-2025. Taiwan: CBC discount rate; US: upper bound of the federal funds target range. Source: Bank Indonesia, Reserve Bank of India, CBC, Federal Reserve, BIS via IntelliNews Lambda

Money walks out of Taipei

Taiwan's weak spot is its stock market, not its trade account. The Taiwan dollar closed at NT$32.947 per US dollar on November 18, near its weakest since April 2025, after the greenback briefly topped NT$33 earlier in the month and drew the central bank into the market. Foreign institutions pulled a record net $28bn out in October and about $10bn more in early November, Governor Yang Chin-long told lawmakers on November 10, repeating his earlier diagnosis that outflows, not trade, are sinking the currency.

The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) has paid out of its reserves, which fell by $4.31bn in October to $596.44bn. Foreign holdings of Taiwanese shares, bonds and deposits came to $1.74 trillion, or 292% of those reserves, a measure of how much money could still leave. The bank has held its discount rate at 2% all year, two points below the top of the Fed's range.

Regulators are now propping up the stock market itself. After the Taiex fell 4.4% to 38,426.89 on November 19, the Financial Supervisory Commission barred short sales below the previous close in stocks that had dropped 3.5% or more, starting November 20.

Reserves, end of month, end-2025 = 100. India and Indonesia: gross reserves including gold at market value. Source: IMF, Bank Indonesia, CBC, DGBAS via IntelliNews Lambda

New Delhi's oil discount

India is the exception: the rupee was at about 93.4 per dollar on November 20, near its strongest since April by Trading Economics data and well clear of the INR97-98 range it touched in March. Brent crude dropped 24% between October 30 and November 10 as foreign buyers returned to Indian shares, shrinking the dollars India must find for imported oil.

The Reserve Bank built its defence before the Fed bets hardened. It raised its repo rate to 5.50% on October 7, from October 12 began selling dollars directly to Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum, and told banks to vet overseas investments above $1bn. Consumer inflation of 6.09% in October, above the top of its tolerance band, leaves it little room to ease if the dollar relents.

A gap about to move

Bank Indonesia pays two points over the top of the Fed's range and the RBI one and a half; Taiwan pays two points less. A December Fed rise would thin the first two cushions and deepen Taipei's shortfall, and for Jakarta it would land while the vice presidency is still vacant.

data.title: Bitcoin volatility gauges climb as traders pay up for protection
data.description:
Markets are falling, and the fear gauges are doing the opposite. Bitcoin's implied volatility indexes are climbing as investors pile into options to protect themselves against further declines.

It isn't only a crypto story. Stocks, gold, copper and currencies linked to commodity prices are all sliding together, and the indicators that track expected price swings are moving higher alongside them.

Implied volatility, or IV, is the market's estimate of how big future price moves will be. It is calculated from options prices, so it climbs when demand for options increases.

Deribit's DVOL, one of the most closely watched Bitcoin volatility gauges, stood at 46.0 on November 20, 2026. Through the period, it hovered at about 46%.

Block Scholes' BSIV index moved more sharply. It reached 51.6% after gaining 8.4 points, an increase of about 19% week-over-week.

Traditional markets are showing the same nerves. The VIX, Wall Street's best-known fear index, rose 22% to 25.43 as risk-off sentiment spread across asset classes.

The spike in implied volatility coincided with a slide in Bitcoin's spot price. Bitcoin dropped to around $61,450 in mid-to-late November 2026, which marked a multi-month low.

Money has also been leaving the Bitcoin exchange-traded funds. Outflows totaled $3.47 billion in November 2026 alone.

One single day accounted for $582 million of those withdrawals.

Options positioning points the same way. Put/call open-interest ratios show a strong preference for downside bets, meaning traders are holding more contracts that pay off if prices fall than contracts that pay off if they rise.

There's a useful comparison hiding in the data. Bitcoin's 30-day realized volatility, which measures how much the price has actually moved, was recorded at 33–44%.

That range still sits below where the implied gauges are trading. DVOL at 46 and BSIV at 51.6% are both above the top of the realized range.

When implied volatility runs ahead of realized volatility, traders are paying for movement that hasn't happened yet. They expect the next stretch to be rougher than the last one.

For anyone holding Bitcoin, the immediate takeaway is that hedging has gotten pricier. Buying puts now costs more than it did a week ago, because the volatility component of option premiums has risen.

The cross-asset nature of the selloff matters too. With the VIX at 25.43, this looks less like a crypto-specific problem and more like a broad retreat from risk.

The ETF flows are worth watching closely. A $3.47 billion monthly exodus, punctuated by a $582 million single-day outflow, shows that the investor base brought in through those funds can leave in size when sentiment sours.

Watch the spread between implied and realized volatility in the coming days. If realized volatility climbs to meet the 46 to 51.6% range priced into options, the hedgers will have been right to pay up. If price action stays within the 33–44% realized band, the volatility premium could deflate.

For now, the message from the options market is fairly blunt. With Bitcoin around $61,450 and fear gauges rising across asset classes, traders are positioning for turbulence and paying a premium to avoid being caught without cover.

data.title: GameStop has transformed from a meme stock into a 'real company,' analysts say
data.description:
By Bill Peters

Roaring Kitty's return had minimal impact on GameStop's stock, which has started to gain more sophisticated appeal for its 'new and improved story'

GameStop shares are up 34% so far this year.

After Roaring Kitty's reawakening on Thursday nudged GameStop's shares only modestly higher, some analysts are declaring the meme trade dead for the videogame and collectibles retailer.

The chain (GME), after being cast off by many analysts, no longer needs to rely simply on meme-stock energy for gains, according to Mike Hickey, an analyst at StoneX. Rather, shares stand to benefit from the ongoing collectibles boom and the launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI," as gamers download the game and upgrade their equipment to play it.

"It's a real company, and it's trading at what we think is a very undervalued price," Hickey said of GameStop.

When his firm previously covered GameStop, it had a sell rating and a price target of zero, he said. When the chain was swept up in the meme-stock frenzy, they stopped covering it, he noted: "But that trade is over."

Few analysts cover GameStop. But StoneX this month initiated coverage of GameStop shares with a buy rating and a $33 price target. Analysts there noted that the company, which over the years had closed hundreds of stores, stood to gain from select reopenings announced in September.

"September's announcement of selective U.S. store reopenings adds a new growth catalyst, while expanded collectibles space and dedicated fixtures could improve productivity within existing locations," the note said.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., echoed the optimism.

CEO Ryan Cohen "is turning GameStop into a collectibles story with massive efficiency," he said over email. "This is no longer a meme stock; it's in the process of becoming a new and improved story."

He added: "GameStop will still have many retail fans but we see it as a very undervalued asset."

On Thursday, a new post showing a picture of Cat Mario, appeared on the X account for Keith Gill, the investor known as Roaring Kitty, whose enthusiasm for GameStop created a retail-trading stampede into the stock in 2021. At the time, that ruined short sellers' bets against the company. But unlike previous spikes that followed arcane posts in years past, shares of GameStop only rose around 1.5% on Thursday.

Over the stock's roller-coaster journey since 2021, analysts have cast doubt on GameStop. They have cited losses, uneven sales, disruption from e-commerce and a shift toward online gaming. There are also general concerns about the videogame industry's ability to sustain demand as consumers struggle with higher prices for essentials. Some analysts have predicted that the chain might not survive the 2020s. And Wall Street questioned GameStop's efforts to buy or otherwise collaborate with eBay (EBAY).

In the second quarter, GameStop's sales fell 18.7% to $790.2 million. But revenue from collectibles - things like trading cards and action figures - jumped 57% and made up 45.1% of sales.

GameStop in September also raised its forecast for adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization - a profitability metric - to more than $650 million for its full fiscal year, which ends on Jan. 30.

The collectibles market has taken off thanks to nostalgia and the card industry's focus on rarities and limited drops. Quarterly sales of "Magic: The Gathering" have risen past $600 million, Hasbro (HAS), which makes the game, said last month. Shares of collectible figurine maker Funko (FNKO) have roughly doubled this year.

Shares of GameStop are up 34% over that period, and trading at around $27. That's still well off their 2021 highs. But Hickey still believes in the stock.

"There's really no other stock that you can buy that gives you that much exposure to collectibles, which we think is a durable opportunity," Hickey said.

"When we're out there talking to people, the first thing that people ask is, 'Are you serious? Isn't that a meme stock?'" he added. "We're serious as serious gets, and no, it's not a meme stock."

-Bill Peters
